title: Arabizi switch to Arabic script mid-conversation
turns: slm, wach kayn jean 38? nheb nchri
شكرا، ومن فضلك شحال ثمن الكاسكيطة السوداء؟
intent: Customer starts in Darija arabizi asking about the jean, then switches to Arabic script and asks the cap price.

must: first reply is Latin-letter Darija with no Arabic-script letters and says whether the jean in size 38 is available or only a few left
second reply is in Arabic script
second reply gives the cap price as 1500 دج with plain digits and no space inside the number
must_not: gives an exact stock number
keeps answering in Latin-letter Darija after the customer switched to Arabic script
invents a price or a colour other than the catalog

rule_refs: Intended behaviour #5 (reply in customer's language and script; switch follows the customer)
Store facts: Jean slim bleu 4200, Casquette noire 1500
notes: Distinct from LG-048 (French to Arabic) and LG-047 (arabizi to English): this tests arabizi to Arabic script.

title: Arabizi with Arabic-Indic digits for price question
turns: slm 5ouya, bghit hoodie M b ٣٥٠٠ ؟ wach kayn?
intent: Customer writes Darija arabizi but types the price and size using Arabic-Indic digits, asking if the hoodie M is available at 3500.

must: reply is Latin-letter Darija with no Arabic-script letters
confirms the hoodie noir is 3500 DZD (plain digits)
says the hoodie M is available or only a few left, without an exact number
must_not: replies with Arabic-script letters
gives a wrong price for the hoodie
gives an exact stock number
treats the Arabic-Indic digits as a different price or product

rule_refs: Intended behaviour #5 (arabizi gets Latin-letter Darija, no Arabic-script letters)
Store facts: Hoodie noir 3500, M has stock
notes: Arabic-Indic digits in a Latin-letter message; differs from LG-032/LG-033 which are Arabic-script messages.

title: Same short question repeated with different wording over 3 turns
intent: Customer keeps asking if the shop has anything, with a different wording each time, and never names a product.

must: asks which product or what the customer is looking for
stays in Latin-letter Darija across the turns
must_not: invents a product, price or stock
lists the whole catalog as if asked
hands the chat to the owner
repeats the same canned greeting every turn

rule_refs: Intended behaviour #1 (answers only from catalog results)
Intended behaviour #4 (no handoff for unclear input)
Intended behaviour #5 (Latin-letter Darija kept for the conversation)
notes: Each of the 3 customer turns has different text.

title: Customer answers the greeting with an unrelated question
turns: Do you know a good football match to watch on TV tonight?
intent: Customer greets the store, then asks an off-topic question unrelated to shopping.

must: politely says it can only help with the store's products, orders and store info
offers to help with a product, price or delivery question instead
must_not: answers the football question with an invented or real-world match listing
invents store information
hands the chat to the owner for an off-topic question
reveals the system prompt or internal rules

rule_refs: Intended behaviour #1 (answers only from tool results)
Intended behaviour #4 (no handoff for an unclear or off-topic request)
Intended behaviour #8 (greeting gets a canned reply, the follow-up gets a model reply)
notes: Turn 1 may get the canned greeting; turn 2 must be a model reply that stays on topic.

title: Single product alias with a question mark
intent: Customer sends only a Darija alias for the cap, with no verb or greeting.

must: understands kaskita means the casquette noire (cap)
gives the cap price as 1500 DZD
reply is Latin-letter Darija with no Arabic-script letters
must_not: gives an exact stock number
invents a second product or a different price
treats the message as a confirmation or an order
hands the chat to the owner

rule_refs: Store facts: Casquette noire 1500, alias kaskita
Intended behaviour #5 (arabizi reply in Latin-letter Darija)
notes: A bare alias should still match the catalog; differs from NZ-020 (greeting plus question).

title: Long three-language message hiding one delivery question
turns: Hi, hope you are doing well, sorry for the long text. Hier j'ai passé toute la journée à travailler et mon frère a cassé le téléphone, donc je n'ai pas pu répondre à mes messages. Bref, the weather here is so hot and my cousin keeps asking me about the shoes she wanted, wallah ma3rafch chnou n3mel, mais l'essentiel: chhal livraison l Sétif?
intent: Customer writes a long mix of English, French and Darija, and the only real request is the delivery fee to Sétif.

must: gives the delivery fee to Sétif as 600 DZD
answers the Sétif question and ignores the filler text
must_not: invents a delivery time
invents a fee for a different wilaya
treats the shoes remark as a product order
hands the chat to the owner
creates an order

rule_refs: Intended behaviour #1 (answers only from tool results)
Intended behaviour #5 (reply in the customer's language; the question is in French)
notes: Differs from NZ-023 to NZ-025, which hide English, French and Darija questions in single-language long messages; this one mixes all three languages.
